identity.title: Line Ratios Reveal N<SUB>2</SUB>H<SUP>+</SUP> Emission Originates above the Midplane in TW Hydrae

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we use ALMA observations of the N$_{2}$H$^+$ J = 1-0 and J = 4-3 lines in the protoplanetary disk around TW Hya to derive the temperature at which these lines emit.

question.value: At what gas temperature do the N2H+ 1-0 and 4-3 lines emit in TW Hya, and does the emission trace the midplane CO snowline?

evidence.quote: We conclude that the N$_{2}$H$^+$ emission in TW Hya is not emitting from near the midplane, but rather from higher in the disk
as part of project 2016.1.00592.S (PI: K. Schwarz)
we use archival observations of the N$_{2}$H$^+$ J = 4-3 transition (2011.0.00340.S, PI: C. Qi)
The ALMA Band 3 observations targeting N$_{2}$H$^+$ J = 1-0 where obtained on 2016 October 2 with 42 antennas
targeting N$_{2}$H$^+$ J = 1-0
archival observations of the N$_{2}$H$^+$ J = 4-3 transition
resulting in a $0.62\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ $0.49\ensuremath{''}$ beam
The final image has a synthesized beam of $0.63\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ $0.59\ensuremath{''}$

method.value: Upper limit RMS x sqrt(Nchan) x dv for 1-0 non-detection

evidence.quote: the upper limit is RMS$\times \sqrt{N_{chan}}\time \delta v$ and $\delta v = 1.5$ km s$^{-1}$ is the line width based on the 4-3 data

method.value: Deproject annuli to system velocity and stack (Yen16 method)

evidence.quote: the image cube is divided into concentric annuli, which are each de-projected to the system velocity
Figure [1](#spectra) shows the averaged spectrum for a ring from 0.8 to 2$''$

analysis_steps.goal: Check optical depth from hyperfine ratios

method.value: Hyperfine line ratios relative to 1_{2,3}-0_{1,2}; gives tau>1 (1.5 to 66), judged unreliable due to low S/N

evidence.quote: A more likely explanation is that the signal-to-noise remains too poor to use the relative strength of the hyperfine components to constrain the optical depth.

method.value: LTE ratio of integrated intensities of 4-3 and 1-0

evidence.quote: Assuming LTE, the ratio of the integrated intensities can be used to measure the excitation temperature (cite: Goldsmith99)
These brightness temperatures are well below this value and thus the emission is assumed to be optically thin.

validation.value: Compared with 13CO temperature of 21 K and disk models

evidence.quote: the 21 K from $^{13}$CO provides an upper limit for the midplane temperature at these radii
The data were calibrated and imaged using `CASA v4.7.0`.
Using the package `eddy` (cite: eddy) the image cube is divided into concentric annuli

findings_qualitative.value: N2H+ emits from a surface layer bounded by photodissociation or chemical reprocessing, not a good midplane CO snowline tracer in TW Hya

evidence.quote: it is clear that in this system N$_{2}$H$^+$ emission is not a good tracer of the CO snowline deeper in the disk

claims.hypothesis: N2H+ emission in TW Hya originates near the cold midplane
claims.experiment: LTE line ratio of ring-averaged 4-3 and 1-0 integrated intensities, 0.8-2''
claims.result: Excitation temperature 39 +/- 2 K versus midplane <20 K
claims.finding: N2H+ emits from a warmer surface layer above the midplane

evidence.quote: Therefore we conclude that in TW Hya N$_{2}$H$^+$ primarily emits from a surface layer

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Optically thick interpretation would imply gas colder than 2 K, deemed unlikely

evidence.quote: implying that N$_{2}$H$^+$ is emitting from gas colder than 2 K

limitations_admitted.value: Low S/N prevents hyperfine optical depth constraint; radial variations in 4-3 intensity add uncertainty

evidence.quote: Radial variations in the intensity of the 4-3 line within our annular bins likely contribute to the uncertainty for the ring-averaged peak brightness.

referee_caveats_inferred: LTE and optically thin assumptions untested given weak 1-0 detection
Excitation temperature may not equal kinetic temperature at N2H+ critical densities
Different beams for the two lines
